scenes.title: Connecticut during the Revolution
scenes.assetBrief: A representative rural Connecticut settlement circa 1777. The exact town and homestead are unresolved, and no figure is identified as a Webb family member.

scenes.title: A missing register is not a disproof
scenes.assetBrief: Representative late-eighteenth-century New England Congregational meetinghouse rendering. It contextualizes the East Hampton Congregational register gap without claiming to depict the exact building or a baptism that has not been found.
scenes.place: East Hampton / Chatham, Connecticut • register context

scenes.title: From Connecticut to western New York
scenes.assetBrief: The dotted connection marks the supported Connecticut-to-Hanover migration corridor; the exact route remains unresolved.

scenes.title: The supported line continues west
scenes.assetBrief: Struck as visually redundant with the Atlas tree. Its evidence contrast is carried by the later proof-boundary scene.

scenes.title: The unresolved parent couple
scenes.assetBrief: James Webb Sr. remains a reported father awaiting decisive original evidence, while the identity of Elizabeth Douglas is conflicted. Neither person belongs in the supported pedigree yet.

scenes.title: Where the public pedigree stops
scenes.assetBrief: A faded England flag marks the theorized older leads, while the Grand Union or Continental Colors reflects the world of James Jr.'s March 1777 birth. The unresolved parents remain separated from the supported frontier at James Jr.
scenes.place: England leads → colonial Connecticut • proof boundary

scenes.title: The records still needed
scenes.assetBrief: Held until actual obtained record images are available. No repository page, register leaf or record montage may be fabricated.

scenes.title: The present edge of the Webb story
scenes.assetBrief: The Connecticut landscape darkens at the supported frontier, without claiming a person, homestead or route beyond James Jr.
